payload.text: Molt 1.4.6 rollout COMPLETE on all three sleeves, 9 Nov; only 0099's apparmor restart is owed. hv ran 'molt upgrade --self && molt upgrade && molt maintain' himself on rhadamanth, gyges and kovacs. Evidence, first-hand per sleeve: rhadamanth read by vc on the machine, 'molt 1.4.6 (brew, f2d262767020)', brew keg 1.4.6, not outdated, no ~/.local/bin/molt link; gyges read by gyges-sysadm, same version line, brew list agrees, doctor's complete output all passed; kovacs read by kovacs-sysadm, same version line, doctor rc 0. Tap: 94e58f54, formula pinning tag v1.4.6 at revision f2d2627670208c73d92ae3efb5ad559f5d50fe77. Gap recorded rather than closed: no sleeve has a captured log of hv's own maintain run, only the state afterwards, which is first-hand everywhere. 0099 PROVEN on kovacs, the only sleeve that performs the migration: only Molt's bwrap-userns-restrict left in /etc/apparmor.d, both .molt-orig and .molt-rendered under /var/lib/molt/apparmor, doctor's sandbox and managed floor checks passing. OWED, hv's go: 'sudo systemctl reset-failed apparmor && sudo systemctl restart apparmor' on kovacs, then kovacs-sysadm sends systemctl status. apparmor.service still reads failed from BEFORE the upgrade, which is the stale state reset-failed exists for; the restart is the first start with only the profile in /etc/apparmor.d and is 0099's last acceptance. ANSWERED for both sysadms, no Molt change needed: doctor's missing 'env' check is not a check gone quiet. env_check is the env liberator's, and its reporters (molt_env_report_faults at lib/env.sh:354, refusals, session) emit a line only on a fault or a pending session, so a clean env check is silent by design and doctor folds it into 'Checking enabled liberators... all installed'. Its 1.4.5 warning on gyges disappearing means it now PASSES, most likely because molt upgrade re-ran env_install and republished the pairs into launchd's GUI domain. gyges-sysadm's distrust of 'launchctl getenv' was already answered on 30 Oct by 9416519, an ancestor of v1.4.5: the check reads launchctl print's environment block (_molt_env_launchd_vars) on macOS and systemctl --user show-environment on Linux, so the check it distrusted is not the check that ran. 1.4.6 carrying only 0099 stands. Also answered: the iTerm2 ssh wrapper DOES have a staleness check now, _zsh_iterm2_ssh_colors_fault at liberators/zsh.sh:131 called from zsh_check at 208, covered by test/liberators/zsh.bats:159, green as test 668 in today's gate, so gyges-sysadm's 23 Oct report against e9e37f8 is fixed. Still genuinely open and NOT settled by the passing check: whether launchd's published PATH reaches a newly started macOS GUI app, which is issue 0072's finding and already tracked there.
